introduction: Who was ‘Abdu’l-Bahá? Bahá’u’lláh’s Will named him the one to whom all must turn and the interpreter of his writings. He himself would accept one title only, “Servant of Bahá,” and spent decades refusing every other that admirers offered. The readings set these two facts side by side: an authority stated in the strongest terms, and a servitude stated in stronger ones. They include his answers to those who questioned his role, his statement that he would obey the House of Justice even against himself, glimpses of his travels in the West, and Shoghi Effendi’s careful definition of his station as neither a Prophet’s nor an ordinary man’s. The Bible offers several successions to compare: Moses and Joshua, Elijah and Elisha, Jesus and Peter. It also has figures who pushed worship away: John the Baptist, Peter with Cornelius, Paul at Lystra, the angel of Revelation. The Buddha’s farewell and Guru Gobind Singh’s disclaimer belong with them. The objections are those raised in the Covenant guides, from Mill, Milton, Kant, Madison and the Bereans, with Peter’s “we ought to obey God rather than men.”
questions: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá is “the authorised Interpreter” whose word is correct, and he asks to be praised “solely for my servitude.” How does each of these make the other believable?
Compare the appointments of Joshua, Elisha and Peter with that of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá. What did the earlier ones leave open?
“Is it right to pray to you?” “No!” Why did he, like Peter with Cornelius and Paul at Lystra, have to keep refusing honours? What does the impulse to exalt a holy person endanger?
“Not one soul has the right to say a word of his own,” and each person must investigate truth for himself. Give an example of each kind of matter.

He said he would submit to an Assembly’s judgement “even if I knew that the judgement was inaccurate.” Socrates stayed in prison; Peter said “we ought to obey God rather than men.” What principle is ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching, and what are its limits?
Shoghi Effendi insists that ‘Abdu’l-Bahá is not a Manifestation of God. What goes wrong, for a community and for the person honoured, when that line is blurred?

outside.why: “Turn your faces toward Him … Who hath branched from this Ancient Root.” The image is Isaiah’s: there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots.
Zechariah: behold the man whose name is The Branch; and he shall build the temple of the Lord.

A written will naming the one to whom all must turn. Moses was told to do it before the whole people: take thee Joshua, a man in whom is the spirit; and thou shalt put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation may be obedient.
A document in the author’s hand. Paul: ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand.
“Whoso turneth towards Him hath turned towards God.” Jesus of those he sends: he that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
Jesus: he that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me.

For whatever is not understood in the Book, he is “the authorised Interpreter.” The interpreter’s work in Ezra’s day: they read in the book distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
An official reading Isaiah in his chariot is asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? and answers: how can I, except some man should guide me?
The Tablet of the Branch refers throughout to “the servitude of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.” Paul of Christ: he took upon him the form of a servant.
The appointment is in “unmistakable terms.” The nearest Christian parallel was spoken, and has been argued over ever since: thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.
Without the Covenant, “a thousand different sects as was the case in former ages.” Corinth: every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas.
In the past “every man with a new idea” attributed it to God. Paul’s farewell: of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
Bahá’u’lláh wished there to be no ground for disagreement. Paul: endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
So he wrote the Book of his Covenant “with His own pen.” The first covenant document: tables of stone, written with the finger of God.
One centre, so that there be no sects. Madison held that liberty is safest where sects are many. What is a religion’s unity for, that a state’s is not?
Moses named Joshua; Christ spoke to Peter “by word of mouth”; Bahá’u’lláh wrote. The word of mouth: feed my lambs; feed my sheep.
The spoken appointment of Peter did not prevent this, a few years later: I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. What does a written and explicit appointment change?
With “no appointed explainer of the Book of Christ, everyone made the claim to authority.” The Second Letter of Peter: no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.
The same letter on Paul’s writings: in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures.
His “highest aspiration” is to be a servant. Jesus: I am among you as he that serveth.
Jesus with a towel and a basin: I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.
A drop, but “connected with the Most Great Sea.” Jesus: as the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine.
“The root of the tree does not bear fruit. The fruit is found upon the branches.” Jesus to those who would come after him: greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.
“Is it right to pray to you?” “No!” The angel in Revelation, when John fell at his feet: see thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant: worship God.
Peter, when Cornelius fell at his feet: stand up; I myself also am a man.
“A thousand souls like me come and go.” Paul: neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.
Paul: we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants.
Look to the Supreme Horizon, “not upon the weak frame of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.” John the Baptist: he must increase, but I must decrease.

“You must not look upon the personality of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, for he will eventually bid ye farewell.” The Buddha, dying, to a disciple who could not bear it: be ye lamps unto yourselves; hold fast to the truth as a lamp.
Jesus prepared his disciples for his own departure in the same way, as something for their good: it is expedient for you that I go away.
Do not grieve at distance from him. Moses was given no shrine: no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
“My name is ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, my title is ‘Abdu’l-Bahá … my reality is ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.” John the Baptist, pressed to say who he was: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness.
He will accept no title but Servant. Jesus refused a lesser compliment: why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God. Why would the greatest be the most insistent on this?
Praise me “solely for my servitude.” A psalm: not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory.
“Pure servitude without interpretation.” Jesus: when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants.
“The servant of the servants of Bahá.” Jesus: whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.
“The visible expression of servitude.” Isaiah: behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth.
“I am free from every title except the title of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.” Guru Gobind Singh: recognize me as God’s servant only.

Praise of any other kind “is contrary to this servant’s religious beliefs.” Paul and Barnabas, when a crowd took them for gods and brought oxen to sacrifice, tore their clothes: we also are men of like passions with you.
One answer to the question of his station, “that all men may be in unity.” Paul: that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you.
“Under the name ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, all perfections are found.” Whitman reached for the largest words for himself: divine am I inside and out. Why would perfection choose the smallest name?
He “closed all doors” against exalted claims on his behalf. Jesus: be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, and all ye are brethren.
“My praise is ‘Abdu’l-Bahá,” the Servant of Glory. Paul chose the same kind of praise for Christ: he made himself of no reputation.
Whatever station he describes for himself, they should affirm that and no more. The Qur’án has Muḥammad say: I am only a mortal like you.
He is “the Interpreter of all the Word and Books.” The risen Jesus on the road: he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

“Whatever he says is correct.” The Catholic Church defined a comparable assurance for the Pope in 1870, within stated limits. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s rests on Bahá’u’lláh’s written word and ended with the line of interpreters. How do the two differ in source and in scope?
In a difference, turn to the verses; in doubt about the verses, to the Interpreter. Isaiah: to the law and to the testimony.

Some “call for reference to verses alone” and ignore the living Interpreter. The Bereans are praised for checking even an apostle against the text: they searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. When is “scripture alone” faithfulness, and when is it a way of setting an appointed authority aside?
“Not one soul has the right to say a word of his own.” Jesus of the Spirit of truth: he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak.

No word of one’s own. Milton thought a living faith produces many: where there is much desire to learn, there of necessity will be much arguing, much writing, many opinions. What kinds of speech is ‘Abdu’l-Bahá ruling out here, and what kinds do the Bahá’í writings elsewhere invite?
He is “the remover of all difficulties.” The Letter to the Hebrews: obey them that have the rule over you: for they watch for your souls.

Kant: have courage to use your own understanding. The Bahá’í writings also command each person to investigate truth independently. Where is the boundary between that duty and the Interpreter’s authority?
“Leave the fabricators and the deceivers.” The First Letter of John: try the spirits whether they are of God.
“I have no opinion of my own.” Jesus: I have not spoken of myself; but the Father which sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say.
Meetings he sanctions bear fruit; others distract. Paul: let all things be done decently and in order.
A prayer recalling that the Covenant was written. Moses had the book of the law laid beside the ark, that it may be there for a witness.
“For thirty years He made mention of the Covenant.” Jeremiah: behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant.
“Capricious souls” begin with whispers. Paul: ye did run well; who did hinder you? A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
Paul gave the churches a plain instruction about those who work in this way: mark them which cause divisions, and avoid them.
Only “those firm in knowledge” draw the meanings. The phrase is from the Qur’án: none knoweth its explanation save Allah. And those who are of sound instruction say: we believe therein.
One says Bahá’u’lláh “has made all independent,” so no Centre is needed. Korah to Moses: all the congregation are holy, every one of them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves?
Miriam and Aaron: hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?
“I do not even claim the station of Peter”; his shelter is Bahá’u’lláh’s. Jesus: I can of mine own self do nothing.
“A word of truth intended for falsehood.” Antonio in The Merchant of Venice: the devil can cite Scripture for his purpose.
From his pen “nothing has flowed except pure servitude.” Jesus: though ye believe not me, believe the works.
“We are all apt to make mistakes. We make mistakes every day.” James: in many things we offend all.
“Without a directing will all would be conquered.” Proverbs: where there is no vision, the people perish.
He holds the wheel “no matter how strong the storm.” The boat on Galilee: he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá is “the ark of the new covenant.” Jesus on the first ark: they did eat, they drank, until the day that Noe entered into the ark.
“The time of the dawning … of the Sun of the Covenant.” Proverbs: the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

“In every movement of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá … there lieth a great wisdom. If what He doeth appeareth to be strange,” it is because the reason is hidden. In the Qur’án Moses asks to follow a servant of God and is told: thou canst not bear with me. How canst thou bear with that whereof thou canst not compass any knowledge?

Trust where the wisdom is not seen. Mill: all silencing of discussion is an assumption of infallibility. Here the assurance is claimed on Bahá’u’lláh’s authority and joined to a life open to inspection. What makes trust of this kind reasonable, and what would make it dangerous in other hands?
His own Will names a successor and asks all to turn to him. The prophets of Jericho, seeing who came back from the Jordan: the spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha.
Elisha took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him.
Paul to his own successor: keep that which is committed to thy trust.
The heir is to be chosen “without regard for the right of primogeniture.” Samuel passed over seven elder brothers for the youngest: the Lord seeth not as man seeth.
After the Founders, dissension; Bahá’u’lláh referred all matters to the House of Justice. Acts: the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.

“I would be the first to obey its command,” though directed against himself. Socrates in prison, refusing to escape a verdict he knew was unjust: he must do what his city and his country order him; or he must change their view of what is just.
“I would submit to it, even if I knew that the judgement was inaccurate.” Paul of Christ: he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death.

Submission even to a wrong decision. Peter before a religious court: we ought to obey God rather than men. Why does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá put the unity of the community above being right in a particular case, and where would the readings set the limit?
“I am the Expounder … expressly appointed.” Of Jesus it was said: he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

The station of Centre of the Covenant was his alone and not transmissible. The Letter to the Hebrews speaks of Melchisedec as a priest without predecessor or successor, a priesthood held by one person and passed to no one.
He comes “after forty-two years of imprisonment.” Paul: my bonds have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel.
“While he suffers from pain, he thinks of our progress!” Paul’s list ends the same way: in weariness and painfulness; beside those things that are without, the care of all the churches.
“My power consists of the Bestowals of the Blessed Beauty.” Paul: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
He was promised help “from his own lips.” Jesus’ last promise: lo, I am with you alway.
Whoever has Bahá’u’lláh with him “is never silenced.” Jesus: I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay.
“How was the end of the persecutors?” A psalm: I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not.
Weak, without belongings or fame, he entered the West, and a verse was fulfilled. The verse: Lo! We have given thee a signal victory.
Paul: God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty.
Wherever he went, people of every rank came to him. The queen of Sheba came to Solomon with hard questions, and said: the half was not told me.
People of every rank were humbled in his presence. The council in Jerusalem before two fishermen: they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
Appointed not “because he is his son but because he is the purest … channel.” John’s Gospel on a kinship that is not inherited: born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, but of God.
“I desire that thou mayst walk in my footsteps!” The First Letter of Peter: leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps.
“Be at peace with all!” Paul: if it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.
“My work is universal.” Marcus Aurelius: my city and country, so far as I am Antoninus, is Rome, but so far as I am a man, it is the world.
A long silence at the window before he speaks. A psalm: be still, and know that I am God.
His letters call souls “to a station which they are potentially able to attain.” Paul: beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, we are changed into the same image from glory to glory.

Shoghi Effendi is exact: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá is not a Manifestation of God and holds no cognate station. The words Christians use of Christ, the express image of his person, belong in Bahá’í belief to Bahá’u’lláh. Why did the Guardian think it necessary to guard this line so carefully against ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s own admirers?
The Centre of the Covenant, the “stainless Mirror” and perfect Exemplar. Jesus to his followers: let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father.

numbers-take-thee-joshua.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him; And set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and give him a charge in their sight. And thou shalt put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may be obedient

zechariah-the-man-whose-name-is-the-bran.text: Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The Branch; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne

corinthians-we-preach-not-ourselves.text: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake
